MECE 4520 introduces data science and machine learning through real engineering systems.

Course materials and source files are available on [GitHub](https://github.com/changyaochen/MECE4520).

## Course focus

Rather than treating machine-learning methods as disconnected algorithms, the course follows a practical engineering progression:

> **understand engineering data → build predictive models → diagnose systems → learn representations → make decisions and control systems**

Students will work repeatedly with a small number of real mechanical-engineering datasets, including gas-turbine emissions and CNC milling tool-wear data. This makes it possible to connect model choices to the systems, sensors, variables, and operating conditions that produced the data.

## Grading policy

The course grade is based on:

| Component | Weight |
|:--|--:|
| Homework assignments | 60% |
| Final project | 40% |

Students should expect approximately seven homework assignments over the semester. The final project will be completed in groups and presented as a five-minute presentation on a selected engineering-data topic.

## Syllabus

This syllabus may evolve as the Fall 2026 course is finalized.

| Week | Topic | Main data or system |
|--:|:--|:--|
| 0 / Pre-course | Python, NumPy/Pandas, linear algebra, and probability refresher | Short exercises |
| 1 | Engineering data, EDA, measurement variability, and essential statistics | Gas turbine |
| 2 | Simple and multiple linear regression | Gas turbine |
| 3 | Statistical inference for regression, prediction intervals, and regularization | Gas turbine |
| 4 | Logistic regression and classification metrics | CNC tool wear |
| 5 | Validation, leakage, grouped splits, and temporal train/test splits | Gas turbine + CNC |
| 6 | Decision trees, random forests, and gradient boosting | Gas turbine + CNC |
| 7 | PCA, dimensionality reduction, and clustering | Gas turbine + CNC |
| 8 | Neural networks and nonlinear function approximation | Gas turbine + CNC |
| 9 | Sequential data, degradation, and optional signal processing | CNC tool wear |
| 10 | Reinforcement-learning foundations: bandits, states, actions, rewards, and MDPs | Mechanical decision examples |
| 11 | Bellman equations, dynamic programming, Q-learning, and SARSA | Gridworld + simple physical systems |
| 12 | Function approximation and deep Q-networks | CartPole + mechanical control |
| 13 | Policy gradients, PPO, continuous control, and RL versus classical control | Pendulum + control systems |
| 14 | Final project presentations | Student-selected engineering system |

## A note on the prerequisites

Introductory statistics will be taught primarily in the context of modeling
problems rather than as a long standalone sequence.

Reinforcement learning and sequential decision-making will receive expanded coverage,
 including when RL is—and is not—a sensible choice compared with
 classical-control approaches.
